| `kube-bench` | `3.2.4` | `cluster` | NIS2 Art.21(2)(i), NIS2 Art.21(2)(g), DORA Art.9, ISO27001:2022 A.8.9 |  | guidance only | No code is generated: the kubelet config belongs to the node image of a managed node group, not to your Terraform. First check the node, because kube-bench also reports FAIL when it cannot read the kubelet config file. The kubelet config needs readOnlyPort: 0 (flag --read-only-port=0). Managed node images set this by default, so a FAIL usually means a custom or old node image. EKS: fix the custom AMI, or set it in the nodeadm NodeConfig (spec.kubelet.config) of the launch template, then roll the node group. GKE: gcloud container node-pools update POOL --cluster CLUSTER --no-enable-insecure-kubelet-readonly-port. AKS does not expose this setting: upgrade the node pool to a current node image (az aks nodepool upgrade --node-image-only). Then re-scan. Caution: Rolling a node group or upgrading a node pool drains and replaces its nodes. |
| `kube-bench` | `4.1.1` | `cluster` | NIS2 Art.21(2)(i), DORA Art.9, ISO27001:2022 A.8.2 |  | guidance only | kube-bench reports this control as manual (WARN). No code is generated: removing a binding can lock out people or break controllers. List the cluster-admin bindings: kubectl get clusterrolebindings -o json \| jq -r '.items\[\] \| select(.roleRef.name=="cluster-admin") \| .metadata.name + ": " + (\[.subjects\[\]? \| .kind + "/" + .name\] \| join(", "))'. Keep the system: bindings of the provider. For each other subject, bind a narrower role, then remove the old binding: kubectl delete clusterrolebinding NAME. On EKS also check access entries with AmazonEKSClusterAdminPolicy (aws eks list-access-entries --cluster-name CLUSTER). |
| `kube-bench` | `4.1.3` | `cluster` | NIS2 Art.21(2)(i), DORA Art.9, ISO27001:2022 A.5.15, ISO27001:2022 A.5.18 |  | guidance only | kube-bench reports this control as manual (WARN). List the roles with \* in apiGroups, resources or verbs: kubectl get roles,clusterroles -A -o json \| jq -r '.items\[\] \| select(any(.rules\[\]?; ((.apiGroups // \[\]) + (.resources // \[\]) + (.verbs // \[\])) \| index("\*"))) \| .kind + " " + (.metadata.namespace // "-") + " " + .metadata.name'. Leave cluster-admin and the built-in system: roles. In your own roles, replace \* with the API groups, resources and verbs the subjects use, then re-scan. |
| `kube-bench` | `4.1.5` | `cluster` | NIS2 Art.21(2)(i), DORA Art.9, ISO27001:2022 A.5.15 |  | guidance only | kube-bench reports this control as manual (WARN). Give each workload that calls the Kubernetes API its own service account. Then stop the token of the default service account in each namespace: kubectl patch serviceaccount default -n NAMESPACE -p '{"automountServiceAccountToken": false}'. Remove RoleBindings and ClusterRoleBindings that grant rights to a default service account. Caution: Pods that still use the default service account lose API access when they restart. |
| `kube-bench` | `4.1.6` | `cluster` | NIS2 Art.21(2)(i), DORA Art.9, ISO27001:2022 A.5.15 |  | guidance only | kube-bench reports this control as manual (WARN). List the pods that do not turn the token off in the pod spec: kubectl get pods -A -o json \| jq -r '.items\[\] \| select(.spec.automountServiceAccountToken \!= false) \| .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name'. For workloads that do not call the Kubernetes API, set automountServiceAccountToken: false in the pod template or in their service account. Caution: A pod that calls the API without a token fails after its next restart. |
